responses.raw_text: Participants discussed distance between parents and children. One reason identified was that parents often do not let children make mistakes; instead, they scold or hit them. A contrasting example was given of a Canadian Pakistani father who allowed his children to make risky choices, even drug use inside the house, because he wanted to know what was going on and wanted his children to feel able to ask him for support when things started going wrong.
responses.speaker: multiple_participants
responses.notes: Sensitive in-person discussion. Public graph should summarize only at theme level and avoid presenting the drug example sensationally.

responses.source_label: In-person meetup: abuse disclosure and family silence
responses.raw_text: The discussion on parent-child distance began from a case where a female was reportedly molested at age 10 by her mother's brother. At age 15, he reportedly tried again, and she understood that what was happening was wrong. She reported it to her mother, but the mother allegedly told her to stay quiet out of fear that the brother would be punished. The participant said the girl later became more spiritual and modest. She had expected to marry a cousin, but the cousin married someone else. According to the participant, this contributed to severe emotional deterioration and later high-risk sexual behaviour through online encounters and casual one-night stands.
responses.speaker: participant_case_report
responses.notes: Highly sensitive allegation and trauma narrative. Do not publish identifiable details. Public graph should anonymize heavily and avoid causal certainty.

responses.source_label: In-person meetup: tarbiyat and parenting readiness
responses.raw_text: Participants discussed lack of education in the sense of tarbiyat. The point was made that parents often do not really know how to be parents. People get married for random or social reasons and then have children as a normal part of the relationship, but they may not accept or understand the responsibility of parenting and therefore do not act accordingly.
responses.speaker: multiple_participants
responses.suggested_theme: Lack of Tarbiyat and Parenting Readiness
responses.notes: Pakistan context. Public graph can use 'tarbiyat' as an Urdu cultural concept, explained as upbringing, character formation, and social-emotional education.

responses.source_label: In-person meetup: rumors and unsupported woman
responses.raw_text: A participant mentioned an orphan woman with no family or relatives. He used to help her with things that needed a man or a second pair of hands, in what he described as a totally platonic relationship. Some people who disliked him allegedly started a rumor that they were having an affair and told the girl he hoped to marry someday. The woman was six years older than him. She reportedly sided with a person she was traumatized from, her boyfriend, when the helper advised her to distance herself. They had two serious arguments about this, and eventually the helper stopped helping her.
responses.speaker: participant_case_report
responses.suggested_theme: Rumors, Social Suspicion, and Withdrawal of Support
responses.notes: Sensitive in-person case. Public graph should avoid identifiable specifics and focus on social rumors, lack of support networks, trauma bonds, and breakdown of trust.

responses.raw_text: All of the in-person meetup topics were discussed in a Pakistan context, except the Canadian Pakistani father example, which was located in Canada.
